scenarios.title: Shaking Starts Indoors
scenarios.description: You're at your desk when the ground suddenly starts shaking hard. There's a sturdy table nearby.

choices.text: Drop to your hands and knees, get under the table, and hold on
choices.feedback: Correct. Drop, Cover, and Hold On is the action recommended by emergency experts worldwide. A sturdy table protects you from falling objects, which cause most earthquake injuries.

choices.text: Run outside as fast as possible
choices.feedback: Running during shaking is how most injuries happen, and the area near exterior walls and windows is actually the most dangerous place in a building.

choices.text: Stand in a doorway for protection
choices.feedback: This is an outdated myth. In modern buildings, doorways are no stronger than the rest of the structure and won't protect you from falling objects.

scenarios.title: Caught Outside
scenarios.description: You're walking outside near some buildings and power poles when the ground starts shaking violently.

choices.text: Move to an open area away from buildings, trees, and power lines
choices.feedback: Correct. If you're already outside, staying outside and moving to open ground protects you from falling debris, glass, and collapsing structures.

choices.text: Run into the nearest building for shelter
choices.feedback: Running toward a building during shaking puts you at risk from falling facades, glass, and debris right as the structure is most unstable.

choices.text: Stand still exactly where you are, even next to a power pole
choices.feedback: Power poles and lines can fall during strong shaking. Move a short distance away from them and other tall hazards while staying outside.

scenarios.title: Driving During an Earthquake
scenarios.description: You're driving when you realize the shaking you feel is an earthquake, not a flat tire.

choices.text: Pull over away from buildings, bridges, and overpasses, and stay in the car
choices.feedback: Correct. Stopping in a clear area away from structures that could collapse, and staying inside the vehicle, is the safest option while driving.

choices.text: Keep driving to get home as quickly as possible
choices.feedback: Driving during strong shaking is hard to control safely, and roads or bridges may be damaged. It's safer to stop in a clear spot until the shaking ends.

choices.text: Stop directly underneath an overpass to wait it out
choices.feedback: Overpasses and bridges are at higher risk of structural damage or collapse during an earthquake. Never stop directly beneath one.

scenarios.title: Shaking at Night
scenarios.description: You are asleep in bed at night when the whole room begins to shake violently.

choices.text: Run outside barefoot as quickly as you can
choices.feedback: Running during shaking is how people fall or get hit by falling objects, and broken glass can cut bare feet.

choices.text: Stay in bed, lie face down, and protect your head and neck with a pillow
choices.feedback: Correct. If you are in bed, staying put and covering your head with a pillow is safer than moving through a shaking room.

choices.text: Stand in the doorway because it is the strongest spot
choices.feedback: The doorway myth is out of date. Modern doorways are no stronger than the rest of the house, and the door can swing and hurt you.

scenarios.title: Aftershocks and a Gas Smell
scenarios.description: The shaking has stopped, but you smell gas in your home and you know aftershocks can follow.

choices.text: Flip the light switch to see what is going on
choices.feedback: Switches can create sparks. Never use flames, switches or electronics near a gas leak.

choices.text: Open a window, leave right away without using switches or flames, and report it from outside
choices.feedback: Correct. Get out quickly, avoid anything that can spark, and report the leak from a safe distance.

choices.text: Stay inside and light a candle to look around
choices.feedback: An open flame near leaking gas can cause an explosion.

scenarios.title: In a Crowded Shop
scenarios.description: You are inside a busy shop when a strong earthquake hits and people start shouting and rushing for the doors.

choices.text: Join the crowd and run for the exit
choices.feedback: Crowds crush and trip people, and the area near doors and glass is dangerous. Hold off until the shaking stops.

choices.text: Drop down, cover your head, and move away from windows, glass and tall shelves
choices.feedback: Correct. Protect your head, stay away from things that can fall or shatter, and wait for the shaking to stop before leaving.

choices.text: Climb onto a counter so you are not trampled
choices.feedback: Getting up on high furniture makes you more likely to fall and be hurt. Stay low and covered.
